extraction_metadata.notes: Extracted from a LinkedIn post about a multimodal chest X-ray report generation system using DenseNet-121 + BioGPT + LoRA on a 6GB GPU. The post's key insight — 'heatmaps alone don't establish clinical correctness' — directly motivates the interpretability-vs-certification theorem card.

title: Can a 6 GB laptop GPU power an AI system that generates radiology reports from chest X-rays?
subtitle_or_tagline: DenseNet-121 + BioGPT + LoRA on a 6GB RTX 3050 — multimodal deep learning for chest X-ray report generation
topic: A multimodal deep learning system combining DenseNet-121 (computer vision, 7×7 grid) and Microsoft BioGPT (347M parameters, pretrained on biomedical literature) to generate chest X-ray reports. Fine-tuned via LoRA (r=16, alpha=32, 0.45% of parameters) on a 6GB RTX 3050 GPU. Achieves 13.4% lower validation loss than GPT-2 baseline (1.77 vs 2.05). Generates reports in 2-5 seconds with Grad-CAM heatmaps and 14 CheXpert pathology classifications.

architecture.data_flow: X-ray → DenseNet-121 (7×7 grid) → Linear Projection → BioGPT (347M) → Report + CheXpert (14 pathologies) + Grad-CAM heatmaps

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Input: chest X-ray image (1024×1024 pixels)
Step 2 - Vision: DenseNet-121 extracts spatial features as 7×7 grid of 1024-dim vectors
Step 3 - Projection: linear projection maps 768-dim visual features to BioGPT's 1024-dim space
Step 4 - Language: BioGPT autoregressively generates report text
Step 5 - Classification: CheXpert classifier predicts 14 pathology categories
Step 6 - Interpretability: Grad-CAM produces heatmaps for visual interpretation
key_claims: 13.4% lower validation loss than GPT-2 baseline (1.77 vs 2.05)
Generates reports in 2-5 seconds per X-ray
LoRA fine-tuning: only 0.45% of model parameters trained
Runs on a 6GB RTX 3050 GPU (consumer hardware)
Data quality matters as much as model architecture
Interpretability matters, but heatmaps alone don't establish clinical correctness
A working end-to-end pipeline teaches far more than training a model in isolation
caveats_or_warnings: This is a research prototype, not a clinically validated medical device or a substitute for a radiologist
Mode collapse was a challenge — improved through dataset rebalancing and vision learning-rate adjustments
Empty generations were a challenge — fixed prompt anchoring and EOS token handling
Anonymization leakage was a challenge — added regex-based output cleanup
GPU memory constraints required LoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning
Heatmaps alone don't establish clinical correctness (author's own insight — this is the gap OSIRIS fills)
